The '''Andorra women's national football team''' ({{langx|ca|Selecció femenina de futbol d'Andorra}}) represents [[Andorra]] in women's [[association football]] and is controlled by the [[Andorran Football Federation]], the governing body for [[football in Andorra]].

==History==
===Background and development===
With a [[FIFA]] trigramme of AND<ref name=never-ranked>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/associations/association=and/ranking/gender=f/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070825202844/http://www.fifa.com/associations/association=and/ranking/gender=f/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 25, 2007 |title=Andorra: FIFA/Coca-Cola World Ranking |publisher=FIFA.com |access-date=23 April 2012}}</ref> and having become FIFA-affiliated in 1996, the national association did not respond to a survey about the status of [[women's association football|women's football]] in the country. In May of the following year, the official who answered another survey from FIFA reckoned that there were 37 active female players, all described as "100% beginners/amateurs". It was further suggested women's football had begun that year in [[Andorra]] and that there had been no previous interest in any women's sport. There was no participation in national or international competitions, though three women were employed in the association.<ref name="williams">{{cite web|url=https://www.dora.dmu.ac.uk/bitstream/handle/2086/5806/Woman%27s%20football,%20Europe%20%26%20professionalization%201971-2011.pdf?sequence=1|title=Women's Football, Europe and Professionalization 1971–2011 |first=Jean|last=Williams|author-link=Jean Williams (historian)|access-date=15 April 2012}}</ref>

As of 2009, the programme was geared for young girls with player registration starting at the age of six.  There were only six women's teams in the country, all for girls under the age of sixteen and includes a national and schools competition.<ref name=goalsprogram2>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2012|publisher=FIFA|url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/goalproject/and_eng.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111125105104/http://www.fifa.com/mm/goalproject/and_eng.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 25, 2011|date=26 November 2008|page=2|title=Goal! Football: Andorra}}</ref> There is also a national women's competition that took place in 2010–11.<ref name=andordaes>{{cite web|url=http://www.fedandfut.com/default.asp?idioma=ang&navpage=page9&doit=page |title=Andorran Football Federation-Women's Football&nbsp;— Senior |publisher=Fedandfut.com |access-date=23 April 2012}}</ref> 16% of the money from the FIFA Financial Assistance Programme (FAP) is targeted at the technical development of the game, which includes women's football, sport medicine and futsal. This compares to 48% for youth football and 25% for infrastructure.<ref name=goalsprogram1>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2012|publisher=FIFA|url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/goalproject/and_eng.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111125105104/http://www.fifa.com/mm/goalproject/and_eng.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 25, 2011|date=26 November 2008|page=1|title=Goal! Football: Andorra }}</ref>

Between 1991 and 2010, there was no FIFA FUTURO III regional course for women's coaching, no women's football seminar held in the country and no FIFA MA course held for women/youth football.<ref name="goalsprogram2" />

As part of the development of the national team, the Andorran Football Federation has a club in the Spanish women's league system with the name of '''ENFAF''', competing in the Catalan Primera Divisió Femení Group 2 as of 2022–23, the sixth tier. Their B team competes in the Catalan Segoba Divisió Femení Group 2, the tier below.

===The team===
On 1 July 2014, the senior team played its first international game in the UEFA Development Tournament celebrated in [[Gibraltar]]. Andorra defeated [[Gibraltar women's national football team|Gibraltar]] by 1–0, scored by Alba at the 61st minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bondia.ad/esports/la-seleccio-femenina-assoleix-una-primera-victoria-historica|title=La selecció femenina assoleix una primera victòria històrica|language=ca|publisher=Bon Dia|date=1 July 2014|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gfa.gibraltarfa.com/women-s-development-tournament.html|title=UEFA Women's Development Tournament|publisher=Gibraltar Football Association|date=13 May 2014|access-date=2 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714144941/http://gfa.gibraltarfa.com/women-s-development-tournament.html|archive-date=14 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> The next day, they played its second international game, losing against [[Luxembourg women's national football team|Luxembourg]] by 4–0.

On 18 December 2014, UEFA announced Andorra would take part in the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2017 qualifying]]. This was their debut competitive match at female football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0252-0cda6c48c9e4-9ddac1575b4e-1000--record-entry-for-women-s-euro/|title=Record entry for Women's EURO|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=18 December 2014}}</ref> In its first official game, the team lost 3–5 to [[Malta women's national football team|Malta]].<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/womenseuropeanqualifiers/match/2016082--andorra-vs-malta/ Andorra 3–5 Malta report at UEFA.com]</ref> Andorra finished the preliminary round with two more defeats against [[Faroe Islands women's national football team|Faroe Islands]] by 0–8 and [[Georgia women's national football team|Georgia]] by 0–7.

On 30 June 2016, the Andorran Football Federation announced [[José Antonio Martín]] as the new head coach of the women's national team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ffandorra.novanet.es/pnfg/NNws_ShwNewDup?codigo=1006745&cod_primaria=3000269&cod_secundaria=3000269|title=Jose Antonio Martín serà l'entrenador de l'absoluta de futbol femení i l'ENFAF sènior femení|language=ca|publisher=Andorran Football Federation|date=30 June 2016|access-date=30 June 2016}}</ref>

On 18 September 2021, Andorra achieved its second win ever after defeating [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] in a friendly match by 4–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.faf.ad/pnfg/NNws_ShwNewDup?codigo=1008277&cod_primaria=3000301&cod_secundaria=3000301|publisher=Andorran Football Federation|language=ca|date=18 September 2021|title=Triomf de prestigi de la selecció femenina a Liechtenstein}}</ref> [[Teresa Morató]] scored a hat-trick, while the fourth goal was netted by Erica Gonçalves.
